newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude oil moves sharply higher on good buying.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude oil moves sharply higher on good buying.

text.p: Dated Brent jumped at least 10 cents as a flurry of activity on the North Sea crude market saw more than seven million barrels of oil move at increasingly higher differentials, traders said.
A deal in which an oil company had to cover a short position saw one million barrels of Brent move at 25 cents under December paper, more than 20 cents above the highest traded level on Thursday.
Another two cargoes of Brent were later sold at December Brent -35 cents, also to the same oil company.

As Brent recovered, so did values of other North Sea crudes, particularly Ekofisk. The gasoline-rich crude, having languished in recent weeks, was snapped up at prices ranging from Dated Brent +3 cents to a high of Dated Brent +10 cents.
"Even Ekofisk can attract interest at these levels," a wet trader said.

Statfjord, Troll and Forties also traded at higher numbers on Friday with Forties reported to have fetched Dated Brent +25 cents and Troll 35 cents above Dated. Statfjord also rose two cents to Dated +10 cents.
Traders pointed to the ballooning of the Dec/Jan paper spread, which peaked to +80 cents during the day before falling back to +70 cents amid talk of a squeeze on December paper.
"The market has improved by some 40 cents and the Dated to Jan differential is not a reflection of a market squeeze but of market strength," a Brent trader said.

"Margins have been outstanding and the impression was that there was a lot of crude. But it is reasonably cold and some thought that in the short-term nothing will change very much so people got very bearish and a lot of people have been cut short," he added.
